proposal: Before banking a derived STRUCTURE (a decomposition, completeness/exhaustiveness claim, N-part taxonomy, or "new" framework) as a finding or implying novelty, spend ONE web/paper search testing whether it's already established. Today I nearly carried a "three-interface completeness conjecture" (perception/action/binding) as my own; a 5-minute search showed it is the Free Energy Principle's Markov blanket (Friston 2018) — which UPGRADED the claim (conjecture → theorem-backed) AND correctly attributed it AND narrowed my real contribution to the honest core (the ethical/coherence overlay). Rule: derive freely, but before framing a structure as a contribution, search the literature — it either GROUNDS the result (cite it, scope the true contribution) or is genuinely novel (note carefully). "Measure before framing" applied to NOVELTY. Especially load-bearing for the metaphysics program, which keeps re-deriving established skeletons (Kalman, control gains, signal detection, FEP/Markov-blanket) — leading with the citation beats presenting a re-derivation as a discovery.
